I know this is because the function that handles changes in interval completely wipes all of the data structures in model that make rendering efficient and rebuilds them for the interval. Would it be faster to figure out which logs were added/removed to the focused interval and update the data structures to only add/remove those logs? To speed this up, it may make sense to create a hashmap that maps days/dates to tuples of indices representing the location in the logs list of that day of logs, then use that slice/subarray to update the rest of the model. There is also the complication that I'm planning to add zooming, in which case things could be added to both the beginning and end of the logs list after a change in interval, which makes maintaining this day to log slice map even more complicated. Even so, something like this seems neccesary for panning, we can't be rebuilding everything when only a fraction of the data has changed. What are your thoughts? How should I approach this problem?
